The largest bone in the human body is the femur.

Regarding the effectiveness of the described physical therapy techniques:

Myofascial release (MFR) is generally considered effective for treating myofascial pain syndrome. By applying gentle, sustained pressure to the fascia, MFR aims to release restrictions in the connective tissue. This can help alleviate pain, reduce muscle tension, and improve the range of motion in affected areas. The technique works by targeting trigger points and adhesions within the fascia, which can contribute to chronic pain and restricted movement. While individual responses may vary, MFR is widely used in physical therapy and manual therapy practices for its ability to promote relaxation and restore normal tissue function.
